artists.biography: Death in Vegas are a psychedelic rock and electronic rock band from the United Kingdom, comprising two permanent members: Richard Fearless (Richard Maguire) and Tim Holmes. Influenced by a wide range of musical genres including psychedelic rock, electronica, krautrock, dub and industrial, the band's sound is constantly changing, moving between live rock sounds, electronica and minimal techno. The band was formed in 1994 by Fearless and Steve Hellier and signed to Concrete Records under the name of "Dead Elvis". Objections from the Elvis Presley estate forced them to change their name, and Dead Elvis became the title of their first album instead.

Death In Vegas.biography: Death in Vegas are a psychedelic rock and electronic rock band from the United Kingdom, comprising two permanent members: Richard Fearless (Richard Maguire) and Tim Holmes. Influenced by a wide range of musical genres including psychedelic rock, electronica, krautrock, dub and industrial, the band's sound is constantly changing, moving between live rock sounds, electronica and minimal techno. The band was formed in 1994 by Fearless and Steve Hellier and signed to Concrete Records under the name of "Dead Elvis". Objections from the Elvis Presley estate forced them to change their name, and Dead Elvis became the title of their first album instead.

perplexity.description:
Dead Elvis is the debut studio album by British electronic band Death in Vegas, originally released in 1997 on the Concrete label. The album is notable for its eclectic fusion of electronic music, dub reggae, hip-hop, techno, and rock, creating a distinctive sound that stood out in the UK's vibrant club scene of the late 1990s. Tracks like "Rocco," "Rekkit," and "Dirt (Slayer mix)" showcase the band's ability to blend heavy basslines, atmospheric textures, and experimental production, often augmented by live instrumentation and guest vocals.

As the first full-length release from Death in Vegas, Dead Elvis established the group's reputation for genre-defying music and set the foundation for their subsequent work. The album received attention for its innovative approach, with critics highlighting its dark, tripped-out atmosphere and its nods to influences such as My Bloody Valentine, The Velvet Underground, and Primal Scream. While not a major commercial hit, peaking at number 52 on the UK Albums Chart, Dead Elvis was recognized as one of the more intriguing electronic releases of 1997, earning praise for its bold experimentation and eclectic style.
